headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.59–1.23), indicating no statistically significant association between Vitamin B1 and bladder cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by moderate heterogeneity (I² = 39.39%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.

sample_size.excerpt: We followed participants in the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study (N = 41,513) for over 20 years and observed 500 UCC cases (89% originating in the bladder; superficial: 279, invasive: 221).

cases.excerpt: We followed participants in the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study (N = 41,513) for over 20 years and observed 500 UCC cases (89% originating in the bladder; superficial: 279, invasive: 221).

effect_size.excerpt: The risk of UCC appeared not to be associated with intake of B-group vitamins or methionine, and findings were consistent across tumor subtypes and across demographic and lifestyle characteristics of the participants. A potential interaction between vitamin B1 and alcohol drinking was observed (all participants: HR per 1 SD = 0.99 (0.91-1.09), never drinkers: HR = 0.81 (0.69-0.97), p-interaction = 0.02), which needs to be confirmed by other studies.

studies.Authors: Boot IWA, Wesselius A, Yu EYW, Brinkman M, van den Brandt P, Grant EJ, White E, Weiderpass E, Ferrari P, Schulze MB, Bueno-de-Mesquita B, Jose-Sanchez M, Gylling B, Zeegers MP

studies.Smoking Status: Never, current light, current heavy, current unknown, former light, former heavy, and former unknown smokers were included and adjusted for

cases.excerpt: Cases were on average older than non-cases (60.3 vs 52.6 years), more likely to be current or former smoker (37.58% and 42.02% vs 20.82% and 29.15%, respectively) and there were approximately three times more male than female cases (2189 vs 726).

effect_size.excerpt: Overall, a decreased MIBC risk was observed for high intake of the vitamins B1, B2, B3, B6, B9 the vitamins related to energy metabolism, oxidative stress reduction and DNA stability (HR B1 : 0.86, 95% CI: 0.77–0.97, HR B2 : 0.88, 95% CI: 0.78–0.98, HR B3 : 0.80, 95% CI: 0.72–0.90, HR B6 : 0.88, 95% CI: 0.79–0.99, HR B9 : 0.86, 95% CI: 0.77–0.96, HR energy metabolism : 0.84, 95% CI: 0.75–0.95, HR oxidative stress : 0.88, 95% CI: 0.79–0.98, HR DNA stability : 0.85, 95% CI: 0.75–0.95) (Table 4 ).
